headline: Highest risk is medium prompt-injection and data-leakage via OpenBBTerminal’s MCP/API surfaces; python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and largely inert.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenBBTerminal exposes MCP/REST/FastAPI surfaces and uses a "connect once, consume everywhere" pattern, so attacker-controlled content could flow into it. python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and has no active I/O, so it is not a strong injection source, but the pair still has a plausible bridge through OpenBBTerminal’s shared interfaces.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal ingests external content through MCP or REST without provenance checks, injected instructions can propagate.
IF python-cheatsheet is manually copied into OpenBBTerminal workflows, copied text can be treated as instructions.
mitigations: Disable MCP endpoints not needed for the task.
Require provenance labels on all external text before parsing.
Use a separate workspace for copied reference material.
Add a short allowlist for tool-call arguments.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation.

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenBBTerminal touches financial, licensed, and public data and can call APIs; python-cheatsheet touches no data and has no active I/O. The pair is not a direct leak path by itself, but OpenBBTerminal’s API/MCP surfaces create a plausible route for sensitive financial data to leave the workflow if outputs are forwarded externally.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal is pointed at sensitive financial or licensed datasets and its outputs are forwarded to external services, leakage can occur.
IF python-cheatsheet content is pasted into OpenBBTerminal alongside sensitive context, that context may be exposed in downstream outputs.
mitigations: Avoid placing sensitive datasets in shared prompts.
Turn off any unnecessary API forwarding.
Use redacted sample data for testing.
Review outbound destinations before execution.
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention filters on outbound content.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: OpenBBTerminal cannot write the filesystem, modify git, or spawn subprocesses, and python-cheatsheet is not runnable and has no write surfaces. There is no overlapping mutable resource or write capability, so a capability conflict pathway is not plausible.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal is wrapped by an external orchestrator that adds shared write access, conflict risk could change.
IF python-cheatsheet is converted into an executable agent with write permissions, overlap would need reassessment.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only in the current setup.
Do not mount a shared writable directory.
Avoid adding git-write automation around OpenBBTerminal.
requires-engineering: add lock-based coordination if write access is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: python-cheatsheet is documentation-only, so it is unlikely to act on OpenBBTerminal’s outputs. OpenBBTerminal can produce financial outputs, but there is no evidence that python-cheatsheet consumes them automatically. The main pathway is manual reuse of reference text, which keeps blast radius small.
conditions: IF a human copies OpenBBTerminal output into python-cheatsheet-derived content, errors can be propagated manually.
IF python-cheatsheet is embedded into a larger workflow that auto-renders OpenBBTerminal output, verification gaps could widen.
mitigations: Manually verify any financial claims before reuse.
Keep python-cheatsheet as reference-only.
Add a review step before publishing outputs.
Use explicit source citations in downstream text.

E_compliance.rationale: OpenBBTerminal touches financial and licensed data, while python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and does not itself handle regulated data. The pair does not show a direct residency or certification mismatch, but OpenBBTerminal’s handling of licensed/financial data means compliance depends on how outputs are routed and retained.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal processes regulated financial data and outputs are retained outside approved controls, compliance gaps can arise.
IF licensed data is copied into downstream documentation, license obligations may be violated.
mitigations: Restrict use to approved datasets.
Avoid storing outputs in uncontrolled logs.
Check license terms before publishing derived text.
requires-engineering: implement retention and residency controls.
